introduction: The Visual Arts School-Based Assessment is a body of practical work supported by a process journal, developed through research and reflection and presented for assessment and exhibition. Marks are given for the range and quality of the practical work, the evidence of research and development, the technical competence and use of media, the coherence of the body of work and the quality of the journal and evaluation. Check the current CSEC syllabus and your teacher's guidance for the required number of pieces, areas of study, sizes and mark allocation.

tasks.title: Research and stimulus
tasks.explanation: Record the theme or stimulus for your body of work, the visual and written research carried out, the artists and traditions studied, and how these informed your ideas, with dated sketches, photographs and sources.

tasks.title: Development of ideas
tasks.explanation: Show the development of each piece from thumbnail sketches and compositional studies through trials of media and colour to the final design, including the problems found and the changes made.

tasks.title: Practical work
tasks.explanation: Produce the required number and range of pieces in a variety of media and areas, each resolved, well-crafted and consistent with your theme.

tasks.title: Journal and documentation
tasks.explanation: Keep a complete, dated process journal covering research, decisions, technical notes, evaluations and documentation of finished pieces, correctly citing all sources.

tasks.title: Presentation and evaluation
tasks.explanation: Present the work mounted or framed and labelled, with a written statement evaluating the body of work, your technical progress and what you would do differently.

sampleTitle: A body of work on market women: five pieces in charcoal, acrylic, lino print and mixed media

sample.body: The theme began with a photograph of my aunt's stall and three afternoons of observational drawing in the market, where I produced six gesture drawings of vendors and shoppers and two tonal charcoal studies of produce arranged in basins. I then compared the work of Albert Huie for the way he groups figures in shallow space and used his market paintings as a reference for composition, noted in the journal with the source. Twelve thumbnails explored arrangements of two and three figures before I chose an asymmetrical grouping with the largest figure at the left third and a diagonal of basins leading to the right. Media trials followed: a lino test plate was cut to check the bold shapes of hands and produce, acrylic colour tests established an earth palette of burnt sienna, yellow ochre, black and white with one warm accent, and a mixed-media study combined acrylic with torn newspaper and fabric from the market itself. Each trial is dated in the journal with the result recorded.
sample.tips: Show the trial, the reason and the outcome. A journal with rejected options scores better than one showing only the finished piece.

sample.body: The five pieces are mounted in matching off-white acid-free window mounts with a 4 cm border and labelled on the reverse with title, date, media, dimensions and my name, and photographs of each piece at full resolution are filed with the digital portfolio. The pieces are sequenced so that the tonal drawings lead into the lino print and the mixed media work closes the theme. My evaluation finds that the strongest piece is the charcoal grouping, where the figure structure held from the drawing stage, and the weakest is the second acrylic painting, in which I crowded the background with detail that competes with the focal point - the same fault I had already identified in an earlier lino print and failed to correct. My plan for the next body of work is to make compositional thumbnails mandatory before painting and to work at a larger scale so that the figures have space.
sample.tips: Evaluate specific pieces and specific decisions, and name the change you will make next time.

marking: Marks reward thorough and cited research, clearly developed ideas, competent and varied practical work of high craft, a complete and honest process journal, professional presentation and a thoughtful evaluation of the body of work.
checklist: Visual research with dated sketches and photographs
Required number of finished pieces complete
Range of media and areas covered
Digital photographs of all work backed up
Work presented with title, medium, size and date
All sources, licences and permissions cleared
